reason: This text passage describes the plagues of Egypt, where Yahweh punishes the Egyptians and Pharaoh to compel the release of the Hebrew people from bondage. The plagues are directed against Egypt, not against the Hebrews. The text explicitly establishes that Yahweh separates and protects the land of Goshen where the Hebrew people dwell (וְהִפְלֵיתִי בַיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת־ אֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן), protecting them from the plague of flies and other afflictions. The Hebrews are portrayed as the oppressed people whom Yahweh is liberating, not as people threatened with death for improper worship. There is no conditional threat or statement in this text about Yahweh killing Hebrews based on their worship practices.
